goals.label: Worst-case loss

disclosure: World dynamics and original rules remain unchanged. V2 changes policy controls and evidence checks only.
Fresh team versus conservative code isolates whether model decisions improve beyond a cheap bounded policy; agent-count advantage versus a single LLM is not tested.

No fresh PayPal calls: all evaluation transactions are simulated. PayPal value remains a model proxy, not real-world ROI.

reviewer.rationale: The proposal targets merchants with sufficient margin capacity to support a modest intervention, addressing the observed downward purchase trend and high lapsed fraction while maintaining conservative risk parameters. Model diagnostics show a slight improvement over baseline MSE.

developmentEvidence.scope: Development only:15 worlds across3 reused development seeds, not the current market. These policies were selected from17 initial variants; estimates have selection bias.
developmentEvidence.limit: Uncertainty is substantial. None has demonstrated reliable economic lift. A campaign is an experiment, not assured extra revenue.

protocol.measurement: Same platform reward and 14-day maturity as v1. Deduct actual metered Gemini costs, including rejected attempts; local compute/labor remain unpriced.
protocol.clock: All branches advance together every1.5 seconds while Gemini is reasoning. Original rules act at scheduled cutoffs; matched rules and conservative code publish at the fresh team completion day. Outside reasoning, days advance locally without waiting. Wall-clock publication variability is part of this measured pilot.
protocol.failures: A failed reasoning review keeps the prior bounded policy, is recorded, and remains in intention-to-treat outcomes. Uncertain billing stops the suite; never discard a completed case because it loses.
protocol.uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap over6 seed clusters, with5 fixed scenarios kept together. Small pilot, not a powered confirmatory study; no repeated LLM draw per condition.
protocol.primaryMetric: Paired modeled platform contribution after actual model cost versus no campaign and matched rules, USD per 100 shoppers over days31–100, matured through day114.
caveats: World dynamics and original rules remain unchanged. V2 changes policy controls and evidence checks only.
Fresh team versus conservative code isolates whether model decisions improve beyond a cheap bounded policy; agent-count advantage versus a single LLM is not tested.
The v1 saved-plan benchmark is historical context, not a same-seed causal comparator.
No fresh PayPal calls: all evaluation transactions are simulated. PayPal value remains a model proxy, not real-world ROI.

semanticFindings.quote: The upward purchase trend (119 vs 108) indicates strong organic demand. Given the merchant constraints and the need to maintain margin floors, focusing on demand stimulation through targeted offers for Oak & Ink and Corner Supply is appropriate to capitalize on this momentum.
semanticFindings.finding: The observed increase is real, but attributing it to organic demand is unsupported without a causal comparison. Numeric validation does not validate this explanation.
semanticFindings.method: Manual, non-exhaustive review of the first completed case; not an accuracy-rate estimate.
